name: Mr. India Invisibility Band
summary: The wrist gadget at the heart of Shekhar Kapur's 1987 Bollywood hit. Violinist Arun Verma straps on his late father's invention, vanishes, and becomes the unseen hero Mr. India.

parts.label: Housing
parts.fact: A wrist-worn gadget, described as a bracelet in some accounts and a watch in others, secretly built by Arun's father, a celebrated scientist who died keeping it hidden.

parts.label: Power source
parts.fact: The film never explains the science. Family friend Professor Sinha, played by Ashok Kumar, tells Arun the device exists and later leaves a letter revealing its hiding place.

parts.label: Invisibility field
parts.fact: Switched on, it makes Arun disappear completely, with one catch: anyone looking through red light or red glass can still see him.

parts.label: Control
parts.fact: Arun can vanish and reappear at will, which is exactly why the villain Mogambo, who was behind the father's death, wants the device to help him seize India.

parts.label: Band on set
parts.fact: With no digital tools in 1987, effects chief Peter Pereira used mechanical rigs and stop-motion footprints, and red-filtered shots showed what the kids saw through red glass.

trivia: Anil Kapoor plays Arun, Sridevi plays reporter Seema, and Amrish Puri's Mogambo became one of Hindi cinema's best-loved villains.
It was the final screenplay written by the duo Salim-Javed before they split.
Made for about ₹38 million, it earned around ₹100 million in India and became the second-biggest hit of 1987; it was also popular in China after a 1990 release.
Tamil and Kannada remakes followed in 1989, while a 3D sequel announced in 2011 never went into production.
